prompt: A split-panel illustration contrasting two eras of phage discovery: on the left, a scientist in muted sepia tones sifts through jars of murky sewage and soil samples under a magnifying lens, searching among scattered natural viral particles for one lucky match to a rod-shaped bacterium, with a small inset showing spiky-headed phages latching onto and bursting a bacterial cell while nearby human, animal, and plant cells remain untouched; on the right, in brighter, sharper tones, a researcher at a computer screen displays a rotating 3D genome blueprint of a phage being actively assembled strand by strand, with a robotic arm or synthesis device constructing a custom phage engineered to match the exact molecular profile of a specific antibiotic-resistant bacterial strain shown beside it, visually emphasizing the shift from hopeful natural discovery to deliberate, on-demand genetic design.
